items.title: Command Line Basics Everyone Should Know | Terminal Tutorial for Beginners
items.description:
Learn the command line from zero: pwd, ls, cd, mkdir, touch, echo, cat, cp, mv and rm, step by step for beginners. Every command was typed into a real terminal and the output you see is the real one, plus the errors you'll hit and how to fix them.

Chapters
0:00 The result
0:26 Why learn the command line?
0:55 Open a terminal
1:30 Where am I? pwd
1:46 What's here? ls
2:49 Move around: cd
3:59 Create folders and files
4:17 Write and read files
4:45 Copy, rename and move
5:42 Delete (carefully)
6:26 Common errors
7:12 Pro tip: Tab and history
7:55 Recap

Open a terminal:
Mac: Command + Space, type Terminal
Linux: the Terminal app
Windows: Git Bash (free with Git for Windows) or WSL

Every command from the video (bash; the $ is the prompt, don't type it):
$ pwd  -  where am I?
$ ls  -  what's in this folder?
$ ls -l  -  one per line, with size and date
$ ls -a  -  include hidden files
$ cd Documents  -  go into a folder
$ cd ..  -  go up one level
$ cd ~  -  go home
$ cd Documents/school  -  several levels at once
$ cd ../..  -  up two levels
$ mkdir trip  -  create a folder
$ touch packing.txt budget.txt  -  create empty files
$ echo "passport" GT packing.txt  -  write a line (replaces the whole file)
$ echo "phone charger" GTGT packing.txt  -  add a line at the end
$ cat packing.txt  -  show what's inside
$ cp packing.txt packing-backup.txt  -  copy
$ mv budget.txt costs.txt  -  rename
$ mv ~/Downloads/*.jpg photos/  -  move every .jpg into photos
$ ls *.txt  -  only the .txt files
$ rm packing-backup.txt  -  delete a file (no trash, no undo)
$ rmdir old  -  delete an EMPTY folder
$ cd "summer plans"  -  names with spaces need quotes
$ history | tail -5  -  your last 5 commands
$ ls --help  -  instructions (on a Mac: man ls, press q to quit)
(GT = the greater-than sign, GTGT = two of them. YouTube doesn't allow that symbol in descriptions.)

Common errors:
No such file or directory  -  check spelling and capitals, run pwd and ls
command not found  -  the command name is misspelled or not installed
File exists  -  pick another name, or just cd into it
cd: too many arguments  -  put names with spaces in quotes
rm: cannot remove 'photos': Is a directory  -  use rmdir for an empty folder

Pro tips: Tab finishes names for you, the up arrow repeats commands, Ctrl+C stops a stuck command.
